$about: Thin strands of smoke rising off a smouldering surface. Data only — no functions, no asset paths. Unknown keys are ignored; invalid values fall back to the defaults in config.ts and are reported in the console.
$emission: The source region sits at emissionHeight above the effect's own origin — position smokewisps.object3d on the smouldering surface itself. Width and depth are full extents; shape point/line/area decides how they are used (a line uses the width axis only). emissionRate is wisps per second; the live population settles at rate x average lifetime and is capped by wispCount, so the rate sets the density and the count sets the budget.
$motion: riseSpeed is the average over a life, not the launch speed: the climb eases out as the smoke cools and mixes. horizontalDrift is a coherent wind every wisp shares, spread is the cone the column opens into, turbulence is the curl written into the strand itself and curlFrequency is how many bends it carries per second of travel. expansionRate widens the smoke as it ages — and thins it in the same measure. maxHeight caps the travel so a long-lived wisp cannot leave the shot.
$look: Widths and lengths are world units at birth; length is applied as a time lag, so a fast wisp is not automatically a long one. softness moves the cross-section falloff from a defined core to pure gradient, noiseScale/detailScale are the two octaves that erode the silhouette and noiseIntensity is how hard they bite. Keep baseOpacity low — density should come from more wisps, not more opaque ones. minScreenWidth is a floor in screen space (fraction of viewport height) that stops distant strands going sub-pixel.
$life: Lifetimes in seconds. fadeInDuration is long enough that a wisp forms rather than appears; fadeOutDuration is long on purpose — smoke dissolves, it does not switch off. randomness is a master on every per-wisp draw: at 0 every wisp is the average of its ranges and the column marches in step.
